# NOTES: *Willow the King: The Story of a Cricket Match* (J. C. Snaith, illus. Lucien Davis; Ward, Lock & Co.)

Dedication: "To my colleagues of the Nottingham Forest Amateur Cricket Club." Contents: 20 chapters plus Epilogue. Narrator: R. C. (Richard Cranford) Dimsdale, club-man of Little Clumpton, batsman, soap-boiler's son, living at late father's place. Only one book in the text (plus publisher ads and footnotes).

## Ch I: The Night Before
- Eve of Little Clumpton v. Hickory match. Team in Dimsdale's billiard-room.
- Nicknamed players: Optimist (Brightside), Pessimist (Grimston), Humourist (Merryweather, "head-ball"), Worry (Daunton, the "Worry", nervous), Treasurer (Scotch mother), Captain (Halliday, corn-cob pipe, milk and soda, gentlest of men), Secretary (Lawson, "Notts", swears, arrives before everyone), General Nuisance (Honourable John Blenkinsop-Comfort, simpers, "Comfort"), Ancient (Oldknow, old, scores steadily, "Old Man" wit), Jessop (Merryweather alt. nickname), Billy (slow bowler, drinks), Charlie (fast bowler, Charlie Trentham), Lennox, Jack Comfort, Jordan, Boulter.
- Trenthams of Hickory: A. H. (Archie, Middlesex, 146 v Surrey), H. C. (Charlie, Cambridge bowler, "best since Sammy Woods"), Captain George (Royal Artillery, 72.3 average), T. S. M. (Tom, Harrow captain), and Grace (Laura Mary, twin of Tom, the sister).
- Hickory also includes Carteret (J. P., "fat short-slip") and Elphinstone (Rev. E. J. H. "Toddles", curate, Kent).
- General Nuisance brings news: Trenthams and Carteret, Elphinstone coming. Conundrum: Why is Bobby Abel batting like Lawson's small talk?

## Ch II: Coming Events
- Dimsdale's man William. Cricket cap "Authentics" lost. Glass wardrobe door smashed; batting practice in pyjamas.
- Wiggles (ground-man) says wicket a billiard table. Dimsdale tempted to press heel on pitch; resists.
- Sportsman newspaper items: Elphinstone 172, Carteret 103 v Notts at Canterbury; A. H. Trentham 97 v Yorkshire at Lord's; H. C. Trentham 9 wickets for 8 (hat trick; bowled Ranjitsinhji); T. S. M. Trentham 205 not out v Gentlemen of Cheshire.
- General Nuisance delivers papers; says Billy drunk (umbrella in bed); Billy's 5-0-51-0 v Emeriti. Muffineer breaks window. Gunter girl (green eyes) engaged to a Trentham.
- William rides 18 miles to Thornhill to borrow his Authentics, returns by 11.

## Ch III: Little Clumpton v. Hickory
- Ground: the Park. Rivalry since 1840s (Mynn, Pilch). Hickory 7 miles away.
- Hickory's four-in-hand driven by Grace in brown holland blouse, white cuffs, Zingari tie, red-and-yellow hat-band. Tests pitch with boots; Wiggles scolds; she tips him a shilling.
- Dimsdale and Ancient practise; Dimsdale drives ball at Grace; she fields with straight arms; catches one.
- Grace bowls to A. H.; Wiggles says "I reckon she's a Trentham."

## Ch IV: An Impossible Incident
- Optimist explains: Grace (Laura Mary), keeps portraits of Archie on mantelpiece; twin of T. S. M. Rector (Honourable and Reverend George Trentham, D.D., giant, ex-bowler).
- Captain George's drive hits pavilion roof; A. H. hits Grace over ladies' tent.
- General Nuisance: Billy confined to bed; Lawson has cabled to Australia for Jones and Trumble. Charlie's mother-in-law ill, Charlie gone to town.
- Players toss: Captain goes out, asks Dimsdale to go in first. Dimsdale put in with Captain.
- Confusion: Hickory has pads on, claims to have won toss. Both sides claim toss; no witness. Toss redone; Halliday calls tails, coin spins; Little Clumpton bats. William arrives with cap.

## Ch V: The Cussedness of Cricket
- Dimsdale and Captain open. Charlie bowls to Captain; Captain plays carefully.
- Grace calls field placements from the coach roof; "Oh, he's a young 'un."
- Dimsdale drives Charlie for four, three, etc.; out l.b.w. to T. S. M. (Tom), "Chuckerrupp!" Scores 7.

## Ch VI: Of a Young Person in Brown Holland
- General Nuisance mocks: offers shilling for cricket outfit.
- Sportsman stats: Dimsdale 10-1-7 scoreboard.
- Optimist brings invitation from Grace. Grace on coach; scoring in black and red ink; Dimsdale described (her brown skin like tea with cream).
- Grace criticises Toddles (Elphinstone) dropping catch; "He'll get a hundred now!"
- Grace: "Oh, I'm so sorry I didn't notice your cap."

## Ch VII: Conversational
- Grace scorns Toddles. Calls Halliday's innings. Score 110 for one. Oldknow (the Ancient) 33, "can't bat a bit." Grace plans to have Charlie bump him.

## Ch VIII: A Cricket Lunch
- Score sheet: Halliday not out 98; Dimsdale lbw b T. S. M. 7; Oldknow not out 46; extras 14; total 1 wicket 165.
- Lunch on coach. Grace's beef sandwiches; champagne ("fizz") from Guv'nor's cellar; toasts: "Here's luck to good old Stoddy in the autumn"; "Good old Archie of that ilk"; "dear old Charlie, and may Stoddy have the sense to take him too." Grace's letter to Stoddart planned re: Charlie's omission. Charlie poured gin by mistake.
- Earl (Dicky, Earl Boughey) and Rector arrive. Grace goes down.

## Ch IX: Record Breaking
- Charlie and Toddles discuss Grace; Earl Boughey as rival suitor; "Bougheys."
- Halliday reaches 100 (after dropped chances), 200 records; partnership with Oldknow.
- Telegram: 267 for one; Halliday 169; Oldknow 72; Grace complains.
- Grace declares she doesn't smoke; "four brothers."

## Ch X: The End of the Day
- Charlie bowls; Halliday out 204 (b H. C. Trentham); partnership 301 breaks record of Barclay and Perkins (1882).
- Oldknow 101 run out (A. H. fielding). Merryweather 28; Dimsdale 7.
- Optimist nervous; Humourist (Merryweather) hits Tom for six; Tom's sister mocks Tom.
- Captain George bowls lobs.
- Final: Little Clumpton 518 for 4 (declared/stumps); Halliday 204, Dimsdale 7, Oldknow 101, Grimston 86, Merryweather 28, Comfort 59, extras 33. Hickory did not bat.

## Ch XI: Cupid Puts His Pads On
- Dimsdale's sleepless night: dreams of brown holland. Grace's name; "damn brown holland."
- General Nuisance (Comfort) visits: "You're in love." Tells him Earl Boughey is rival; Grace holds "at-homes first Monday and third Friday."
- Dimsdale's sister Mary (returned from town), "Ricky" family name. Asks about Laura Trentham and slang.
- Dimsdale walks to Hickory Rectory, sees Grace batting in single-wicket on lawn; Stoddart (Archie) and others. Gloucestershire v Middlesex match arranged; Dimsdale selected to play for Gloucestershire.

## Ch XII: My First County Match
- Middlesex v Gloucestershire at Rectory. Grace (W.G.) captains Gloucestershire. Archie breaks library window. Father (Rector) measures distance; Archie's bat ("A Warsop"). Rectory rules: rule seven (out if you break window); cucumber frame controversy; Grace kisses Toddles' hat (Harlequin cap) oath dispute.
- Tea: strawberries; Rector's tobacco plants and tigridias ruined by cricket ball; curl in the air; Rector a D.D. (Cambridge gave for bowling).
- Tom's fight with gooseberry bush.

## Ch XIII: A Case of Heredity
- Curl in the air hereditary (from Rector). Grace's cross bat. Tom selected for Kent match Monday at Tonbridge; telegram "Hooray! Isn't A. J. just a darling!"; Grace replies "Shall be very glad to play, Tonbridge, Monday. T. Trentham."
- Optimist bowled by Grace's curl. Grace bowled Dimsdale-free; Gloucestershire wins by one wicket. Dimsdale stays to dinner.

## Ch XIV: In Which I Am More Sinned Against Than Sinning
- Dinner; Charlie and Dimsdale fight with soap; Toddles, Carteret, Optimist tease Dimsdale into proposing. Bet: Carteret lays "pony" Dimsdale won't. Dimsdale goes to library.

## Ch XV: Facing the Music
- Grace in library working averages from telegrams; "Dimmy" nickname. Dimsdale proposes badly; Grace misses it; telegram from Oval, Taunton, and third telegram: "Hawke for India... You are going with me. Stoddart." (Charlie chosen.)

## Ch XVI: A Telegram from Stoddart
- Telegram text: "If Hawke wants you for India, sing slow. You are going with me. Stoddart."
- Grace excited; Dimsdale blocks door; Pearson on the Creed thrown. Grace suggests Dimsdale play single wicket tomorrow: if she beats him he's out; if he beats her she considers his claims.

## Ch XVII: A Few of Its Consequences
- Group in dining-room playing baccarat; celebration; Rector celebrates; Jennings the butler; champagne ("Miss Laura had it yesterday"). Rector: King Charles II slept in Chamber.
- Optimist and Dimsdale in room. Dimsdale tells Optimist of proposal.

## Ch XVIII: I Receive Instruction in a Heart-breaking Science
- Optimist: "Can you bowl?" Dimsdale's bowling "putrid." Grace coaches him; Biffin the umpire (Biffin hit on head by ball). Grace bowls "devil"; "I shall give you a most awful licking."

## Ch XIX: A Case for M.C.C.
- Umpire dispute (Biffin); Grace insists. Father stands as umpire instead. Dimsdale batting first. Borrowed kit: Carteret's buckskins, Charlie's shirt, Archie's unmentionables.

## Ch XX: A Case for Another Eminent Authority
- Dimsdale bats: 23 runs; Optimist drops him at mid-on. Dimsdale bowls poorly. Grace 20+; Grace deliberately knocks down her wicket to declare ("There's no declaration law in the Rectory rules"). Biffin: "Hout, sir, fair hout!"

## Epilogue
- Morning Post marriage notice: "On the 11th inst., at the Parish Church, Hickory... by the Rev. E. J. H. Elphinstone, M.A., Richard Cranford, eldest son of the late William Dimsdale, to Laura Mary ('Grace'), only daughter of the Honourable the Reverend George Trentham, D.D., Rector of Saint Mary's, Hickory."

## Publisher ads and footnotes (back matter)
- Ads: Guy Boothby, G. J. Whyte-Melville, Henry Kingsley, Joseph Hocking, E. Phillips Oppenheim, Windsor Magazine.
- Footnote A: Daily Chronicle disproved the "please/thank you" claim. Footnote B: "crowd" at Oval, "company" at Lord's. Footnote C: the toss incident is true, came within the writer's experience.
